ch15.d.A: Distance $A$ the block is pulled from equilibrium before release
ch15.d.k: Stiffness $k$ of the spring; larger means more force for the same displacement
ch15.d.m: Mass $m$ of the block on the spring
ch15.d.damp: Drag force proportional to velocity; light: damping ratio $\zeta = 0.05$
ch15.d.vectors: $\vec v$ and $\vec a$ of the point on the circle, and $v$, $a$ of the block (vertical parts)
ch15.goal.proj: Simple harmonic motion = the projection of uniform circular motion onto one axis
ch15.goal.props: Properties of a harmonic oscillator: the period does not depend on the amplitude, $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, $K + U$ is constant
ch15.obs.phase: Graphs: $v$ leads $x$ by $90^\circ$; the speed is largest at $x = 0$ and $v = 0$ at the turning points
ch15.obs.a: The $a$ graph is the $x$ graph flipped and scaled by $\omega^2$ ($a = -\omega^2 x$): the vertical part of the centripetal acceleration on the circle
ch15.obs.iso: Amplitude 0.1 m → 0.3 m: the period $T$ stays the same (isochronism)
ch15.obs.km: $k$ times 4 or $m$ divided by 4: $\omega$ doubles, the period halves
ch15.obs.energy: Energy graph: $K$ and $U$ trade every half period; their sum $E = \tfrac{1}{2}kA^2$ stays constant
ch15.obs.space: Phase space ($x$, $v$): a closed ellipse traced clockwise; with damping, a spiral into the origin
ch15.obs.damp: Light damping: the amplitude and $E$ decay exponentially; the period barely changes
ch15.assume.spring: Ideal massless spring; $x$ is the displacement from equilibrium (gravity only shifts the equilibrium)
ch15.assume.scale: Arrows on the circle: $v$ scaled by $1/\omega$, $a$ by $1/\omega^2$. The phase-space $v$ axis is scaled so that $A\omega$ always spans the same width
ch15.n.d.theta0: Angle $\theta_0$ from the vertical at release
ch15.n.d.L: Distance $L$ from the pivot to the centre of the bob
ch15.n.goal.small: Small angles: $\sin\theta \approx \theta$, so the motion is SHM with period $T_0 = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$
ch15.n.goal.large: Large angles: the restoring force grows more slowly than $\theta$, so the period is longer and depends on the amplitude
ch15.n.obs.ghost: Dashed bob: the SHM model released from the same angle; the real pendulum falls further behind each swing
ch15.n.obs.10: Release angle 10°: the two bobs nearly coincide ($T/T_0 = 1.002$). 90°: $T/T_0 = 1.18$. 150°: 1.76
ch15.n.obs.L: Four times the length: twice the period, the same $T/T_0$
ch15.n.assume: Massless string (a massless rod beyond 90°), point bob, no air resistance, $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$. Drawn scaled to $L$, so every length looks the same
